claim: Uniqueness for sampled supercritical small-epsilon cases
evidence: 5/5 sampled cases have stable Beyn rank one and converged S0/S1 moments, stable candidate, tighter-contour check and one certified fixed-M mode; 5/5 also pass off-grid BIE + decay checks.
limitation: Finite numerical sampling supports, but does not prove, theorem-wide uniqueness.

claim: Local mode existence for sampled supercritical small-epsilon cases
evidence: 5/5 have explicit singular-vector and equilibrated certificates plus configured physical diagnostics.
limitation: Local existence support does not imply a converged global count.

claim: Leading asymptotic sigma = C(a) epsilon^2 + O(epsilon^3 |log epsilon|)
evidence: On epsilon <= 0.1, relative error of sigma/epsilon^2 from C(a) changes from 0.097% at epsilon=0.02 to 5.560% at epsilon=0.1; Q range [0.0461, 0.902].
limitation: Bounded Q on a finite sample is numerical consistency with the Big-O remainder, not a proof of the asymptotic estimate.

claim: Non-existence on sampled subcritical small-epsilon geometries
evidence: 4/4 sampled subcritical cases have no resolved interior mode; zero-supported cases use an independent whole-band absolute-SVD scan when Beyn rank is contaminated by the cutoff.
limitation: Numerical non-detection has a finite resolution floor and is not a mathematical proof of absence arbitrarily close to the threshold.

evidence: 4 epsilon values bracket the zero/one transition; (a_c-a0*)/epsilon lies in [-0.04219, -0.03516] with maximum final a-bracket width 9.375e-04.
limitation: Finite epsilon values demonstrate bounded sampled scaling, not a limit proof.

claim: Numerical implementation sensitivity at fixed M
evidence: finite_difference_step at fixed M=24: max delta_sigma=1.113e-07; harmonic_order at fixed M=24: max delta_sigma=5.957e-09; lattice_terms at fixed M=24: max delta_sigma=4.268e-09
limitation: Fixed-M one-at-a-time sensitivity is representative, not exhaustive over every geometry; no mesh-convergence claim is made.

claim: Analyticity in epsilon and epsilon log epsilon
evidence: The code reports numerical consistency with the leading expansion but does not test analyticity.
limitation: Analyticity is a theorem-level functional property and cannot be established from finitely many numerical samples.
